newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says bond income not considered an economic activity.
newsitem.headline: Court says bond income not considered an economic activity.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday the mere acquisition and holding of bonds for income is not an economic activity and does not create a taxable status.
If income from bonds derives merely from holding them, that interest cannot be regarded as a return on an economic activity or a transaction carried out by the bondholder, the court explained.
"The activity of a bondholder may be defined as a form of investment which does not extend further than straightforward asset management," the court said.
Although the VAT directive includes the "exploitation of intangible property for income", it also exempts "transactions in shares, interests in companies and other securities," the court said.
The court found no reason to treat bondholding differently from shareholding.
"VAT - Interpretation of articles 4, 13 and 17 of Sixth directive 77/388/EEC - Taxable person - Acquisition and holding of bonds"
Reference from the Hoge Raad der Nederlanden for a preliminary ruling in the proceedngs pending before that court between

on the interpretation of articles 4(2), 13B(d)(5) and 17(3)(c) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)

Article 4(2) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment is to be interpreted as meaning that the mere acquisition of ownership in and the holding of bonds, activities which are not subservient to any other business activity, and the receipt of income therefrom are not to be regarded as economic activities conferring on the person concerned the status of a taxable person.
